guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 7 April 2009 sets out the terms in a section headed "Loan/credit conditions and covenants" and repeats them in its data sheet. There was no condition of loan effectiveness: the document states "Loan Effectiveness Condition: There is no loan effectiveness condition." Three covenants went into the Project Agreement. One carried a date: for the Ethnic Minority Cultural Heritage Protection component, Guizhou "shall cause a Community Project Management Group and a Village Supervision Group to be established at each of the selected minority villages by September 15, 2009, with terms of reference, staffing and other resources acceptable to the Bank", as set out in the Operation Manual for Community Participation. The second required Guizhou to carry out the project in accordance with that manual, to send the Bank any proposed amendment to it for prior approval, and to put into effect only amendments agreed with the Bank. The third required Guizhou to cause the project participants to implement Guidance No. 30 of 2007, issued by the Guizhou Provincial Party Commission and the provincial government on 28 November 2007, on safeguarding the interests of ethnic minorities and their cultural heritage in the development of rural tourism and ensuring that ethnic minorities receive the benefits of it. On money, the appraisal document states that "No specific financial management covenants are applicable to the project except for those standard financial covenants such as project audit and interim financial reports". No covenant about land acquisition or resettlement appears among the three. The consolidated Resettlement Action Plan and the Resettlement Policy Framework were prepared for the project under the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy, so the rule the renovation at Huangping Jiuzhou broke was a rule of the project's own framework, not one of the covenants the appraisal document prints.
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P091950, 7 April 2009: section III.F "Loan/credit conditions and covenants", paragraphs 47-50, repeated verbatim in the data sheet under "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any". Financial covenant sentence: Annex 7 (financial management), paragraph 34. Consolidated RAP and RPF: paragraph 64. The Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004154 of 18 December 2017 prints no covenant-compliance table; its footnote 7 and paragraph on the Huangping Jiuzhou renovation place the temporary-resettlement requirement in the RPF.

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 14 April 2011 sets the terms out in a section headed "Loan/credit conditions and covenants" and repeats them in its data sheet. Money for the first disbursement category, which covers the civil works, goods, consultant services and training, could not be drawn until three things were done: the Subsidiary Agreement had been executed on behalf of the Kunming Municipal Government and the Kunming Rail Transit Company; that agreement had been duly authorised or ratified and was legally binding on both of them; and the company "has secured the land required for metro - public transport - bicycle integration according to the Integration Plan, in form and substance acceptable to the Bank". The implementation covenants required the company to prepare and send the Bank, by 15 February each year from 2012, a proposed action plan for that year's works, with the scope and schedule of activities, the financing plan and detailed budget arrangements including counterpart funds validated by the city, for the Bank's review and approval; then to carry out the works in accordance with the plan the Bank had approved; and to get the Bank's prior concurrence for any change to or waiver of the plan. Separate reporting requirements obliged the company to send the Bank half-yearly reports on implementation of the Environmental Management Plan and the Resettlement Action Plan, semi-annual progress reports by 15 February and 15 August each year from August 2011, and a mid-term review report by 31 December 2012. On money, the appraisal document states that "No specific financial covenants are applicable to the project except for standard financial covenants, e.g., project audit and interim financial reports". The Resettlement Action Plan appears in the reporting requirements; no covenant in the section requires it to be carried out.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P117656, 14 April 2011: section III.E "Loan/credit conditions and covenants", disbursement conditions and implementation covenants (a)-(c), repeated verbatim in the data sheet under "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any". Reporting requirements: section III.F, paragraph 40. Financial covenant sentence: Annex 7, paragraph 27. `land` is tagged for the disbursement condition requiring land for the integration works to be secured before the works category could be drawn on.

hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 23 April 2012 prints the terms as a table of nine "Legal Covenants" in its data sheet, each recurrent and yearly, binding each of the three provincial implementing entities. Three are about land and people. Each entity "shall, apply and caused to be applied the measures and actions set forth in its RAP in a timely and efficient manner satisfactory to the Bank" - its Resettlement Action Plan. Each "shall carry out measures for improving the living standard of Displaced Persons affected by the Project, and include provisions into the implementing contracts entered into for the implementation of the project" to ensure the environmental codes of practice and the environmental management plan were met. And no entity may "amend, suspend, fail to enforce or waive the applicable RAP, ECOP, PMP, EMP, EMDP or any annual implementation plan without the prior written approval of Bank". A fourth required each entity to "engage and retain the services of independent consultants to carry out external monitoring and reporting, and implement the recommended measures" - the third-party monitoring the completion report's demolition figures come from. The rest are administrative: maintain a provincial project leading or coordinating group, a provincial project management office and a county project management office; carry out the works in accordance with the Project Implementation Plan and the Project Agreement; implement the environmental codes of practice and pest management plan, with Gansu also implementing its ethnic minority development plan and Hunan its environmental management plan; send the Bank an annual implementation plan by 31 December each year from 2012; and apply the Financial Management Manual. The completion report records that the interim financial reports were submitted late and so "not in compliance with financial covenants in legal documents", and that procurement was carried out in accordance with the legal covenants.
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P118597, 23 April 2012: data-sheet table "Legal Covenants", all nine entries (Project Implementation Arrangement; Project Implementation Plan; Safeguards Framework-RAP; Safeguards Framework-ECOP and PMP; Process Framework; Monitoring and Reporting; Implementation; Annual Implementation Plan; Financial Management Manual). The document prints no "Conditions" table, so no condition of effectiveness or disbursement is recorded. Compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004709, 24 September 2019, paragraphs 102 and 103.

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 10 May 2012 prints the terms as a table of six "Legal Covenants" in its data sheet, and under the heading "Conditions" it records "Not applicable", so no condition of effectiveness or of disbursement was attached. Two of the six are about money. Before the first disbursement to a project county, the World Bank loan proceeds had to be on-lent to it "on terms and conditions satisfactory to the World Bank". The borrower had to "Ensure adequate funding for counterpart requirements", a recurrent yearly covenant. The other four are administrative: maintain the project management and implementation units throughout implementation with qualified and adequate staff; submit the annual work plan to the Bank for its no objection by 15 December each year; conduct a mid-term review by 31 August 2015; and complete a Project Operational Manual cleared by the Bank by 30 August 2012. None of the six names land acquisition or resettlement. Resettlement action plans for the Wanzhou and Wushan sites were prepared, submitted to the Bank on 19 January 2012 and found acceptable, but the covenant table does not require them to be carried out. The documents are explicit about the limits of what the loan obliged anyone to do after the landslide. The completion report's post-closing annex states that the emergency preparedness and response plan "was not prepared for the World Bank-financed project, and the World Bank's role is limited to the provision of technical support in the review process as part of a 'no regrets' risk management contribution by the World Bank". Of the further livelihood support the Bank's mission discussed for the resettled household, the same annex says it "is not part of the RAP entitlement matrix. Rather, this is a 'beyond compliance' suggestion".
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P126210, 10 May 2012: data-sheet tables "Legal Covenants" (six entries: Project Management and Implementation Units; Counterpart Funds; On-lending agreements; Annual Review of Work plan; Mid-Term Review; Project Operational Manual) and "Conditions" (single row reading "Not applicable"). RAPs prepared and accepted: section IV.E, paragraph 55. The two quotations on what was not required: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004869, 29 October 2021, Annex 6 "Post-Closing Report for the Outstanding Environmental and Social Issues", paragraph 3 (EPRP) and paragraph 10 (beyond-compliance suggestion). The absence of a resettlement covenant rests on the data-sheet covenant table being the appraisal document's own complete list of the loan's legal covenants.

xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 20 May 2013 prints the terms as a table of two "Legal Covenants" and one "Condition" in its data sheet. The condition was one of effectiveness: the loan could not become effective until Xuancheng Municipality, through the development zone, entered into a Subsidiary Agreement with the zone's construction and investment company. The first covenant carried the date 30 June 2014: the company "shall have entered into a contract for the construction, and at least 5 years of operation and maintenance, of the wastewater treatment plant of the Project, with an entity or entities duly qualified to perform such tasks, all under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank", cited to Section IV.A.1 of the schedule to the Project Agreement. The second is a cost-recovery covenant, recurrent and yearly: "For each of the Borrower's fiscal years starting 2018, the Wastewater Treatment Plant, should have total revenues equivalent to not less than its total operating expenses, excluding depreciation", cited to Section IV.A.2. The completion report states that "All the legal covenants were complied with on time." Neither covenant names land acquisition, house demolition or resettlement. The resettlement action plan of April 2013 and a Resettlement Policy Framework were prepared, the framework because the sites of the later land sales to industry were not yet known. For plots sold after the loan's closing date, the appraisal document records not a requirement but a promise: "the client has agreed that any land acquisition and resettlement activities will be undertaken in a manner consistent with the provisions set out in the RPF".
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, P129431, 20 May 2013: data-sheet tables "Legal Covenants" (two entries, citing Project Agreement Schedule Section IV, A.1 and A.2) and "Conditions" (one entry, type Effectiveness, Subsidiary Agreement). RAP and RPF, and the "client has agreed" sentence: section IV.F, paragraphs 63-65, repeated in Annex 3, paragraphs 50-52. Compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005311, 23 February 2021, paragraph 97. The absence of a resettlement covenant rests on the data-sheet covenant table being the appraisal document's own complete list.

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.conditions_add: The emergency project paper of 22 January 2009 sets the terms out in a section headed "Terms and conditions for project financing". Nothing was required before negotiation, Board presentation or effectiveness: both lines read "None". Four things had to be done before money could be drawn: payment of the front-end fee; adoption by Sichuan and Gansu provinces of the Operations Manual, including the Environmental and Social Screening and Assessment Framework and the Financial Management Manual; approval of sub-projects by the Bank and by government; and adoption of the Procurement Plan by the two provinces. Because the sub-projects were not chosen when the loan was approved, that framework is where the obligations on land and people sit. The implementation covenants required the provinces to maintain the provincial project leading groups, the project management offices and the local project implementing units throughout the project; to "apply the OM, the ESSAF and the FMM in carrying out the project"; to ensure sub-projects met the agreed eligibility criteria and were prepared taking the Bank's comments into account, and, where the Bank's prior review was required, to implement them only after the Bank had approved them; to "implement sub-projects in accordance with implementation plans to be prepared, and plans to mitigate any adverse environmental and social impacts to be prepared pursuant to the ESSAF"; and to carry out capacity building and technical assistance in accordance with proposals approved by the Bank. The framework itself, the document says, sets procedures for identifying eligible project-affected people, determining compensation, exploring and implementing rehabilitation measures, and management and monitoring. That last covenant is the one the Moba Gorge forest-land payment of 650 yuan per mu fell short of: the plan the Bank had approved set 1,744 to 3,160 yuan per mu, and the completion report says the compensation "was below agreed rates".
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.why: World Bank Emergency Project Paper, P114107, 22 January 2009: section G "Terms and conditions for project financing", paragraph 105 (the conditions for negotiation, effectiveness and disbursement and the five implementation covenants (a)-(e)), repeated in the data sheet; Annex 7 (financial management and disbursement), paragraph 12, repeats three of the four disbursement conditions. What the ESSAF covers for resettlement: section IV.F, paragraph 86. Non-compliance: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003783, 27 February 2017, paragraph 49 ("below agreed rates and is being rectified by GPG") and Annex 6. Note for the checker: the data sheet's line "Significant, non-standard conditions, if any: None" sits immediately above the same four disbursement conditions on the same page, so it is not read here as denying them.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.conditions_add: The works at Zhamushui were added to an existing loan, and the published terms belong to the original 2002 agreement. The appraisal document of 30 May 2002 made one thing a condition of loan effectiveness: execution of the subsidiary loan agreements between the government and Hubei province, and between Hubei and the project companies through their prefecture and county governments, satisfactory to the Bank. Bank approval of the environmental management plans for the transmission lines was a condition of disbursement for the matching expenditure categories. Hubei had to maintain a project management office with terms of reference and resources satisfactory to the Bank, and to on-lend the loan to the project companies on the same terms as the Bank loan, with the companies carrying the foreign exchange risk. On land and people, Hubei had to "cause each of the project counties to enter into arrangements satisfactory to the Bank with the project company located in such county" for the resettlement, compensation and rehabilitation of all persons affected by its part of the project "in accordance with the respective RAPs and RPFs", and equivalent arrangements for environmental mitigation under the management plans. Each project county had to set up a poverty alleviation enhancement fund and put into it 20 per cent of the fiscal revenues the project brought the county, for at least five years after operations began. Before the first generating unit was commissioned a project company had to open a debt service reserve account and pay all net revenues into it until it held the next six months' principal and interest. Those covenants name the four original project companies and counties. The Guangrun component was added by an amendment to the Loan Agreement in July 2006, with its own Project Agreement prepared in January 2007; neither the completion report of 14 June 2012 nor the 2018 performance assessment prints what that agreement required. A resettlement plan for Guangrun dated 7 December 2005 was prepared.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, China - Hubei Hydroelectric Development in Poor Areas Project (P068049, Loan 4666-CHA), 30 May 2002, section G "Main Loan Conditions": the effectiveness condition (subsidiary loan agreements); agreements reached with Hubei province (project management office; on-lending with foreign exchange risk; involuntary resettlement arrangements in accordance with the RAPs and RPFs; environment; poverty alleviation enhancement plans by 31 December 2003 and the 20 per cent fiscal-revenue fund); agreements reached with the project companies (debt service reserve account). Disbursement condition on transmission-line EMPs: Annex 6 (disbursement arrangements), paragraph 4. Phase boundary: Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR0000339, 14 June 2012, paragraphs 15-16 (July 2006 Loan Agreement amendment, January 2007 Guangrun Project Agreement) and Annex 5, paragraph 4 (Guangrun RAP dated 7 December 2005); Project Performance Assessment Report 127227, 18 June 2018, paragraphs 2.3 and 3 and the Guangrun section. This document was fetched in this round from the World Bank documents API and saved as /home/claude/r22/cache/P068049_PAD.pdf and .txt. Excluded under the ordinary-commercial-terms rule: the 1.2 debt service ratio, the 80:20 debt-to-equity limit, the 20 per cent working-expenses-to-revenues ratio and the dividend restriction, all in the same section.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.conditions_add: The appraisal document of 12 February 2004 sets the terms out in a section headed "Main Conditions". Nothing unusual had to be done before the loan took effect: the entry reads "Standard conditions of effectiveness". The covenant that bears on the resettlement is in the road network part: "Wuhan shall carry out the EMPs, RAPs and the RPF, in a manner satisfactory to the Bank, in particular: (a) Prior to commencing any work not included in the RAP, prepare a RAP in accordance with the RPF", and the same for environmental management plans. That is the covenant under which the resettlement plan for the Sanjintan to Ping'anpu section of the Middle Ring was prepared in July 2007, three years after appraisal. The same part barred Wuhan from changing the agreed road programme unless the change was compatible with the Wuhan Urban Transport Strategy and a full feasibility study acceptable to the Bank had been carried out. Wuhan also had to maintain, until the project was finished, a Municipal Project Leading Group with terms of reference acceptable to the Bank, and a Project Office with units responsible for land acquisition and resettlement, environmental management, procurement, financial management, construction management, project management and monitoring and reporting, "adequately resourced with suitably qualified staff"; to keep the construction supervision team in place for the whole implementation period; and by 30 November each year from 2004 to send the Bank a proposed annual work programme and budget for comment and then implement what was agreed. It had to furnish semi-annual progress and procurement reports, annual reports by 15 February each year from 2005, and hold the mid-term review by 31 May 2006; to have its accounts audited each year by independent auditors acceptable to the Bank; to have the road maintenance management system in place by 31 December 2006; and to review the road maintenance reform, the public transport reform and the transport strategy with the Bank once a year.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.why: World Bank Project Appraisal Document, Wuhan Urban Transport Project (P069852), Report No. 25590, 12 February 2004, section G "Main Conditions": G.1 effectiveness ("Standard conditions of effectiveness"); G.2.1 accounts and audit; G.2.2 monitoring, review and reporting; G.2.3.1 implementation overall (Municipal Project Leading Group, Project Office with a land acquisition and resettlement unit, annual work programme, construction supervision team); G.2.3.2 road network development component, items (i) and (ii)(a)-(b); G.2.3.3 road maintenance; G.2.3.4 public transport; G.2.3.5 technical assistance. The plan the resettlement covenant produced: Resettlement Action Plan for the Sanjintan - Ping'anpu Section of the Middle Ring (RP603), 1 July 2007. No completion report for this project is in the cache; the Independent Evaluation Group review ICRR13574 of 27 June 2011 prints no covenant-compliance table, so compliance is not cross-checked here.
